report.summary: Home's nine sections, the three frozen demo runs and the bundled authored default pack, served through a new FixtureReader that getReader() picks whenever no repo was found; RunDetailBody extracted so the proof section renders the real run page.

friction.detail: The refactor demo-run predicate ('at least two BatchReports with differing remainingSiteKeys lengths') matches almost nothing in this repo's history: a refactor run only reaches 'passed' once every batch resolved, so every passed run's remaining counts are all zero. Exactly one run qualified and its manifest predates a config-key rename, so the script wrote nothing. Relaxed to two batches and two batch reports, keeping the plan's drop measurement and tie-break unchanged, and said so in the script.

Several old manifests no longer parse (`agentCommands` renamed to `agent-commands`), so getRunView threw for the top-ranked candidates. Each slot now walks its ranked candidates and takes the first whose view assembles, logging every skip and its reason; the 'a slot with no qualifying run fails loudly' behaviour is unchanged.

The plan specifies reading VITE_SITE_ORIGIN through `import.meta.env`. ts-jest compiles this package to CommonJS, where `import.meta` is a syntax error, and homeMeta is loaded by the route-tree suite — so the whole suite would fail. Implemented as `process.env.VITE_SITE_ORIGIN` with a `define` in vite.config.ts, which reads the same in all three toolchains. Both the reason and the mechanism are commented in place.

The plan's Jest mapper note covers only `.gif`; FixSection imports six workflow SVGs with `?url`, which Jest also cannot load. One combined `\.(gif|svg)(\?.*)?$` entry, placed ahead of the `#assets` rule because Jest stops at the first matching pattern.

`getStandardsPackBundle` already existed from phase 1 at `views/common/utils/`. Rather than create a second one at the path this plan names, the existing file was moved to `views/getStandardsPackBundle.ts`, given the required sort, and its two importers repointed.

'fixtures by side then path' is implemented as the declared FixtureSide order (pass, then fail) rather than alphabetically — alphabetical would put the counter-example first and would flip the order three existing tests pin.

listings.json carries no slug, so ProofSection maps slug to row with a three-entry predicate map mirroring the freeze script's own slot criteria. Reading getDemoRunViews() there instead would have pulled a quarter of a megabyte of run detail into the chunk the lazy boundary exists to keep it out of.
The plan does not name the three proof-panel tab labels; used 'A clean run', 'A refactor burn-down' and 'A run that stopped', since a run's own title says nothing about why it is in the frame.

No unit tests written for the two new .mjs scripts. freezeDemoRuns needs a local `.lightsout/` run history that CI does not have, and buildDefaultPackView is guarded by `check:default-pack` in CI and the pre-push hook. Other scripts in this repo do carry tests, so this is a gap worth naming.
`NotFound`'s 'Back to runs' link points at `/`, which is now Home rather than a runs list. Left alone as outside this phase's scope; the wording will want revisiting when the runs table lands.

reports.summary: No tests written: the only subject, packages/web-app/src/defaultPackAsJson.d.ts, is an ambient TypeScript declaration file (`declare module '#assets/default-pack.json'`) with no runtime logic — it emits no JavaScript, so it can neither be imported by a test nor appear in a coverage report; the standards' files-that-must-not-have-dedicated-tests rule covers exactly this case, and its three siblings (sprawlDatasetAsJson.d.ts, demoRunsAsJson.d.ts, markdownAsText.d.ts) likewise carry no tests. The type it declares is exercised at typecheck time by getDefaultPackBundle, whose own test parses the committed assets/default-pack.json against StandardsPackBundle.

friction.detail: The assignment listed a .d.ts ambient declaration as both the test subject and the changed internal that must execute under coverage. Those two demands cannot both be met: a declaration file has no emitted code, so no test can make it appear in a coverage report. The task's coverage-verification gate will report this file as unexecuted no matter what is written. Non-emitting files (.d.ts) should be filtered out of the changed-file list before subjects are assigned.

Chose to report complete with zero test files rather than invent an indirect test through a non-subject consumer (getDefaultPackBundle), because the rules forbid creating a test file for any file outside the subjects list.

reports.summary: No test file written: the only subject, packages/web-app/src/demoRunsAsJson.d.ts, is an ambient type-only declaration file (four `declare module '#assets/demo-runs/*.json'` blocks with a single `const` + `export default` each) — it holds no executable logic, compiles to nothing, and the standards' files-that-must-not-have-dedicated-tests rule bans a dedicated test for it; jest.config.cjs already lists declaration files in collectCoverageFrom so it reports zero statements rather than going missing, and it cannot fail the execution gate. Audited the two modules that consume the declared specifiers and are the only way the declarations are exercised — src/lightsout/common/utils/getDemoRunViews.unit.test.ts and getDemoRunListings.unit.test.ts — both already parse the committed fixtures against the engine's RunView/RunListing contracts and assert concrete output values (slug key set, per-slot status and pipeline, step count, runId agreement across both accessors, newest-first ordering, memoisation identity); no toBeDefined()/not.toThrow()-only paths were found, so nothing was added or strengthened. Sibling declaration files src/markdownAsText.d.ts, src/sprawlDatasetAsJson.d.ts and src/defaultPackAsJson.d.ts carry no tests either, so this matches the repository's existing precedent.

friction.detail: The assignment listed a `.d.ts` ambient declaration file as both the sole test subject and the sole changed internal. A type-only file has no public runtime surface to test through, and the standards forbid a dedicated test for it, so the two rules in the task (test every subject / every changed file must execute under coverage) cannot both be satisfied by writing a test. Chose to write nothing, audit the existing consumer tests that exercise the declared module specifiers, and report complete — rather than fabricate a test file for a non-testable source file or create a test for a non-subject.

changedFiles.summary: added a process.env + jest.isolateModules setup factory and four tests covering the previously unexercised branch where VITE_SITE_ORIGIN is set — og:image absolute against the deploy origin, og:url with and without a trailing slash via test.each, the other four tags surviving alongside them, and an empty-string origin treated as no origin

reports.summary: Extended the existing homeMeta test to cover the set-origin arm of the og:image/og:url ternary (previously only the unset arm ran) plus the trailing-slash and empty-string edges; the four pre-existing tests are unchanged apart from contentOf gaining an optional meta parameter that defaults to the module-scope homeMeta, so their assertions are untouched; no files were skipped.

friction.detail: The plan specifies VITE_SITE_ORIGIN is read through import.meta.env, but the implemented source reads process.env (its docblock explains that Jest compiles the file to CommonJS where import.meta is a syntax error, and that vite.config.ts substitutes the value at build time). I tested the source as written, arranging the variable with jest.replaceProperty(process, 'env', ...) — the pattern already used in packages/engine/src/views/listStandardsPacks.unit.test.ts.

packages/web-app/jest.config.cjs maps every .gif/.svg import to tests/stubs/styleUrl.ts, so the sprawl GIF's URL is the stub's '/assets/app.css' under test rather than a fingerprinted build path. I asserted og:image with a regex pinning the absolute origin and a non-empty path instead of an exact string, so the test pins the contract (absolute URL joined to the deploy origin) rather than the stub's value.

changedFiles.summary: added a test reading the authored default pack by name on a repo whose config names no pack — the exact call scripts/buildDefaultPackView.mjs makes — pinning built: false and the type-assertion rule's fixture sides and paths, so a bundle that came back with an empty proof cannot be committed to assets/default-pack.json

reports.summary: Audited the three subjects' existing co-located tests (getStandardsPackBundle.unit.test.ts, getStandardsPackRuleView.unit.test.ts, getStandardsPackView.unit.test.ts) against every branch of getStandardsPackBundle.ts, getStandardsPackRuleView.ts and getStandardsPackView.ts: the sortBundle documents/rules comparators, both arms of the fixtures side-then-path comparator, the found and not-found arms of the name lookup, and both projections plus their two typed not-found errors all already execute, and every assertion pins a concrete output value or a typed error class rather than toBeDefined()/not.toThrow() — so no assertion needed strengthening and no healthy test was rewritten. Verified the brittle numbers the existing tests pin against the pack on disk (111 rules, 52 checked, 24 documents, 111 with both fixture sides, channels base/nestjs/react/tanstack, type-assertion's 2 pass and 1 fail fixture) — all correct. Added the one missing path: no test read the default pack through getStandardsPackBundle, only through its two sibling views, leaving the call the committed default-pack bundle is built from unpinned. Skipped no files; wrote no test file for any non-subject.

friction.detail: getStandardsPackView.unit.test.ts (a subject's test file) also carries a describe('listStandardsPacks') block of three tests, while listStandardsPacks.unit.test.ts exists beside it with nine different ones. The standards call a test file spanning several source files a split candidate, one subject per file, but moving those three would be deliberate cleanup with its own review rather than a side effect of this task, and listStandardsPacks is not in my subjects list. Left in place and reported here.

The plan states getStandardsPackBundle sorts so that assets/default-pack.json is byte-stable across APFS and ext4, but the sort is unobservable from disk today (every folder reader already sorts what readdir handed it, as the source docblock says). I pinned the observable contract — the resulting order — rather than forcing the reordering itself, which no input reachable through the public surface can produce.

changedFiles.summary: added a setup factory and three tests — the authored default pack is read live (absolute rootPath) rather than replaced by the committed snapshot in listPacks and getPack, and a process made public after a repo was found is answered by the fixtures on the next call
added a test pinning the remaining empty-standards fields — no `at` timestamp, `path: '.'` and an empty trend

reports.summary: Audited the existing co-located tests for all seven subjects; every changed internal already executes under them (InProcessReader through getReader.unit.test.ts, DemoRunSlug through getDemoRunViews and FixtureReader). Strengthened two gaps: getReader's tests proved only the pack name for a repo whose config names no pack, which is true whether the pack was read live or served from assets/default-pack.json, so the default-pack substitution predicate's negative case (isDefault && !built) had no assertion — now pinned for both listPacks and getPack via the absolute-vs-repo-relative rootPath; and getReader's documented 'fresh instance per call' contract had no test, now pinned by flipping LIGHTSOUT_PUBLIC after a repo was found. FixtureReader's empty StandardsView left `at`, `path` and `trend` unasserted; now pinned. No test file created for DemoRunSlug.ts — a pure constant with no runtime logic, which the standards say must not have a dedicated test; it is covered through getDemoRunViews and FixtureReader. findRepoRoot.ts changed only in a doc comment and its existing test already covers every branch including LIGHTSOUT_PUBLIC, absolute/relative/empty LIGHTSOUT_REPO, the walk and the walk reaching the filesystem root.

friction.detail: The plan's scope says 'give every created component and util a co-located test', but packages/web-app/src/lightsout/common/constants/DemoRunSlug.ts is a pure `as const` object with no runtime logic, which the standards' files-that-must-not-have-dedicated-tests rule forbids testing directly. Followed the standards and covered it through getDemoRunViews and FixtureReader instead.

Every subject already had a co-located test written during implementation, so this run was the audit path: no new test files, only added assertions where a changed branch's contract was unpinned. Verified statically rather than by running the suite, since the role forbids running tests.

changedFiles.summary: added two tests reaching ProofSection's unexercised branches — the runs link's label while the repo query is still pending, and a demo slot no frozen run fills — plus the setup-factory parameters and the two module stubs (a never-settling repo-root server function, a swappable getDemoRunListings) those cases need

reports.summary: Audited the three subjects' existing suites: RunsIndex.unit.test.tsx already covers both the repo-found and no-repo branches plus the run-count singular/plural split with real output assertions, and InstallLine.unit.test.tsx already covers the command text, the copy affordance and the className passthrough — neither was missing a changed path, and no assertion in either was a bare toBeDefined/not.toThrow, so both were left unchanged. Home.unit.test.tsx covered the composition and nine section headings but seeded the repo-root query in every case and used the committed listings unaltered, leaving two ProofSection branches — the `data?.repoRoot` optional chain before the query resolves (plan Decision 27) and the `listing === undefined` slot drop — reachable through no test; both are now exercised through Home. The remaining changed internals (HeroSection, SlopSection, FixSection, FiveThingsSection, SprawlSection, BurnDownSection, QuickStartSection) execute through Home's existing render and also carry their own co-located suites. No files were skipped as untestable.

friction.detail: DemoRunDetail.tsx is listed as a changed internal reached through Home, but Home.unit.test.tsx deliberately mocks it to null with a documented reason: the React.lazy chunk in ProofSection resolves partway through the suite, so the real component's headings appear in some tests and not others and the nine-section heading assertion becomes order-dependent. I left that mock in place rather than destabilising the subject's suite — DemoRunDetail executes under its own co-located suite in the same coverage run, so it still appears in the report.

All three subjects already had co-located suites, and the two coverage gaps I found belong to ProofSection, a changed internal with its own test file that I am not permitted to touch. I closed them through Home, the subject that owns ProofSection, which required parameterising Home's setup factory (a swappable getDemoRunListings and an opt-out of seeding the repo-root query) rather than adding cases to ProofSection's own suite.

The package's committed coverage report (packages/web-app/coverage/coverage-summary.json) is stale — it predates this phase, listing the now-deleted getRepoRoot.ts and none of the features/home files — so it could not be used to locate uncovered branches and the gaps had to be found by reading each component's branches against its test file.

changedFiles.summary: added two tests through the Home page covering the standards section's showcase-card states — the pending placeholders while each rule's text is still being read, and a card dropped when the pack no longer carries that rule — plus a controllable getPackRule stub and a notFound entry on the router mock the rejection path reaches

reports.summary: Audited every listed subject and changed internal against the tests already on disk. Home.unit.test.tsx, RunDetailBody.unit.test.tsx, the six RunDetail scenario suites and router.routeTree.unit.test.tsx already execute all eight changed files and assert real output values: the three linksDisabled branches in RunHeader, StepCard and StepReportSummary are each pinned both ways in RunDetailBody.unit.test.tsx, RunDetail's query/planPath/PlanDrawer composition is pinned by RunDetail.unit.test.tsx and RunDetail.plan.unit.test.tsx, and routes/index.tsx and routes/repo.index.tsx are driven through router.routeTree.unit.test.tsx (head, loader and component). The one real gap was StandardsSection's ShowcaseRule, whose pending and query-failed branches no test reached; both are now covered through the Home surface. No new test file was created; no file was skipped as untestable.

friction.detail: routes/repo.index.tsx's head() (returning [{ title: 'Your repo' }]) is the one changed line left unpinned. Route files may not have co-located tests, so the test that owns them is router.routeTree.unit.test.tsx — which sits at 394 lines against the blocking test-size-file cap of 400. Adding the assertion pushed it to 404, and the alternatives (splitting the suite, or a new router.routeTree.repo.unit.test.tsx duplicating its ~120-line setup factory) are both cleanup work outside this task. Reverted the addition; the module still executes and its loader and component are asserted, so only that one arrow function is uncovered.

StandardsSection is a changed internal with its own pre-existing co-located test file, so the two missing branches could have gone there. The assignment's rule that internal coverage is earned through the owning public surface won, and both tests were added to Home.unit.test.tsx instead.

The plan specifies reading VITE_SITE_ORIGIN through `import.meta.env`. ts-jest compiles this package to CommonJS, where `import.meta` is a syntax error, and homeMeta is loaded by the route-tree suite — so the whole suite would fail.
